memo.verdict: Neutral; park. Addlife (ALIF.B-SE) at SEK 170.7 (2026-09-23) is a self-help case that has largely delivered and now asks to be re-classified as a compounder; the shares already pay for the deal pace consensus models, so the 'Modal return' is about 7 percent a year over eighteen months and about 9 percent a year over three years with the like-for-like multiple held, an F against the framework's 20 percent bar. Conviction medium on the direction (every multiple branch but the unlikely compounder one, about 14 percent, is below the bar) and low on the level (Triaging depth; three brokers; a consensus EPS series with a basis break). The gate line is not triggered: management C, business quality C, predictability B, trackability C; the case is parked on the return. Entry level about SEK 130 to 145 (the case clears the bar below about SEK 128 at three years and SEK 144 at eighteen months on the modal multiple; about SEK 138 and SEK 154 with the post-amortisation multiple held at 27.9x). Re-entry at a higher price only on four or more deals announced in the six months to March 2027 at stated margins above segment averages with leverage at or below 2.5x on the company's definition. Alarm levels: adjusted EBITA margin below 12.5 percent in any quarter other than Q3; leverage above 2.5x at year-end 2026; cash conversion below 80 percent of EBITA for FY2026; organic growth below 3 percent for two quarters; fewer than four deals announced in the six months to March 2027. Invalidate levels: leverage above 3.0x sustained; adjusted EBITA margin below 12 percent for two consecutive quarters; acquisition multiples above 8x EV/EBITDA or earn-out targets missed; organic growth below 2 percent for two consecutive quarters.
case: The thesis: a 2022 change of chief executive and finance director turned a leveraged post-pandemic distributor into a disciplined one, and the outputs prove it. Adjusted EBITA margin 11.3 percent (FY2024) to 12.1 percent (FY2025, excluding the SEK 158m gain) to 12.6 percent (Q2 2026), ten consecutive quarters of expansion; net debt to EBITDA 4.2x (2023 peak) to 2.2x (end-2025) on internally generated cash; Camanio closed (SEK 50m to 60m of annual cost; SEK 100m impairment in Q4 2023), AddVision's headquarters dismantled (saving more than SEK 20m a year), the UK endoscopy business sold on 1 December 2025 for SEK 158m against SEK 140m of annual sales; return on working capital 62 percent in 2025 against a 45 percent target; cash conversion about 100 percent of EBITA over the last twelve months.

The change has travelled all six layers of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain, which is why the market has priced it: people (the executive pair, a refreshed board, an expanded central M&A team), choices (margin before volume; niche deals below EUR 50m at below 7x), actions (exits, pruning, six bolt-ons since April 2025), key operating metrics (margin; working-capital return), financial statements (FY2025 operating cash flow SEK 1,392m, +27 percent; H1 2026 EPS +17 percent) and sell-side estimates (an upgrade to Buy in February 2026; estimates up 1 to 3 percent after Q2 2026). The shares re-rated on the balance sheet from about SEK 151 before the Q4 2025 results (3 February 2026) to SEK 164.90 by 20 April 2026 and SEK 170.7 now (+26.4 percent over six months); the EV/EBITA discount to Asker narrowed from 27 percent (January 2026) to 8 percent (April 2026). The contracted catalysts are already priced; the price moved with the news.

The external forces are a modest net tailwind, not an inflection. European Medtech grows about 3 percent a year (2024 to 2028) and clinical diagnostics 2 to 3 percent; group organic growth 6 percent (2024), 3 to 4 percent (2025), 3 percent (Q1 2026), 4 percent (Q2 2026). The strongest external force, MDR and IVDR compliance (deadlines end-2027, 2028 or 2029 by class; notified-body approval rising from 10 to 90 percent of diagnostic tests), pushes small owners to sell (95 percent of 33,000 to 38,000 European Medtech companies considered relevant targets) and so feeds the acquisition pipeline rather than demand; rated B. Macro is a D headwind: translation cut H1 2026 sales by SEK 113m and EBITA by SEK 13m (about 2 percent each), FY2025 sales by SEK 310m and EBITA by SEK 46m; a percentage point of rates moves the financial net by about SEK 40m; net EUR outflow SEK 1,008m and USD outflow SEK 406m in 2025. Spain (16 percent of Medtech) lost surgical volume to doctors' strikes in every month of Q2 2026; the UK (18 percent of Medtech) had subdued capital sales. Competition for customers is rational (tenders won above competitors' prices); competition for targets is tightening (Asker's 12 acquisitions in 2024; Palex with Apax entering nine markets; Addtech's nine continental deals), offset by target multiples softening to below 7x. Eastern Europe is the one region of state-backed demand growth (Poland's 8 percent of GDP target by 2027). The Swedish serial-acquirer group's valuation is itself a force: a 13 percent multiple contraction over the year to June 2026, small-cap outflows, Asker's Sell downgrade.
counter_case: At its strongest, the risk research's "False Friend", which wins its own analysis-of-competing-hypotheses matrix with zero hard inconsistencies against five for the bull case. The margin recovery is tail-cutting and a cyclical rebound in eye surgery and Homecare rather than structural improvement, so absolute EBITA growth stays near 10 percent a year while the footprint shrinks and the margin flatters. The acquisition programme is opportunistic and integration-free: a former Head of M&A (13 March 2024) describes "a pure reporting shell" with no integrated IT and 29 countries without central controls, and says that "without extracting synergies, large acquisitions simply add massive overhead costs"; a former Vision Ophthalmology Group chief technology officer (22 April 2022) says the deals "brought no operational synergies"; a former executive (25 April 2025) says opportunistic deals diluted the Labtech moat and the current team lacks deep diagnostics expertise. So returns on capital stay at a distributor's 10 to 11 percent while the shares are priced at a compounder's multiple. A working-capital slip in a slow-paying European hospital system (receivables SEK 1,597m at end-Q1 2026; 44 percent of European businesses collecting beyond 60 days; H1 2026 working-capital outflows of SEK 377m) pushes leverage from 2.6x (2.8x gain-adjusted; 2.89x lease-inclusive) back toward the 3.0x ceiling, which stops the deals, as it did in 2022 to 2023, with only about SEK 0.5bn of headroom and an LTIP that rewards 20 percent a year EBITA growth. The multiple is an industry multiple resting on the serial-acquirer label, which the market has just withdrawn from Asker (Sell downgrade on earnings quality, 10 September 2026; -31.6 percent over twelve months; 0th percentile of its own history) and is withdrawing from the group (multiples down 13 percent to mid-2026; Addtech downgraded on its premium to Lifco); it contracts to 13x EV/adjusted EBITA, giving about SEK 105 (DNB Carnegie's bear range SEK 100 to 150), a fall of 38 percent, or to the ten-year "crash" band of 16.40x, -41 percent on the dashboard's basis. The evidence for this is the one thing three separate research reports agree on: return on capital employed 11.0 percent in 2025 against Asker's 14.8 percent and Lifco's 20 to 25; net working capital 12.3 percent of sales against Asker's 8.4 percent; the 15 percent target missed in three of four years; the H1 2026 cash outflows; Asker's de-rating showing the market's willingness to withdraw the label. And the case cannot be disproved from the accounts, because the company does not guide, the consensus rests on three brokers whose EPS basis changed during the year, and the deal pace that would settle it takes at least a year to prove.

The record concedes: adjusted EBITA growth on its path is 10 percent a year, not 15; the returns are a distributor's; the decentralised model forgoes integration by design, so the deals must be bought right to pay; the drop-through half of the EPS growth is reversible; management has not shown high-volume acquisition execution; the market is not rewarding the pattern. The record does not concede that the outputs are false: ten quarters of margin expansion across both segments, leverage cut from 4.2x to 2.2x on cash the business generated, cash conversion about 100 percent of EBITA over the last twelve months, and deals priced below 7x with earn-outs are facts, not framing. The record's response is that the counter-case and its own view converge on the recommendation: the counter-case argues for avoiding the shares at this price, and so does the record, for the milder reason that the return is below the bar even if the bull case is right on the operations; the competing hypothesis does not need to be right for the case to fail. Where the counter-case would win outright: a cash or margin disappointment in the next two quarters, which the record puts at about 35 percent, and which would take the multiple toward 20x post-amortisation and the return to about nil.
triggers: - Entry level: about SEK 130 to 145 (the bar clears below about SEK 128 at three years and SEK 144 at eighteen months on the modal 26x; about SEK 138 and SEK 154 at 27.9x held); the shares traded near SEK 151 after the Q1 2026 miss and the 52-week low is SEK 128.86.

- Re-entry at a higher price: four or more deals announced in the six months to March 2027 at stated margins above segment averages with leverage at or below 2.5x on the company's definition; this would move the compounder branch (30x, about 14 to 18 percent a year) from unlikely toward plausible.

- What would change the record's mind on the acquisition pace: the same four-plus deals by March 2027; what would confirm the counter-case: fewer than four (alarm), or multiples above 8x EV/EBITDA or missed earn-outs (invalidate).

- Margin: two consecutive quarters below 12 percent invalidates; below 12.5 percent in any non-Q3 quarter is the alarm; absolute adjusted EBITA falling while the margin rises would confirm the tail-cutting reading.

- Cash and leverage: Q4 2026 leverage above 2.5x on the company's definition, or FY2026 cash conversion below 80 percent of EBITA, is the alarm; leverage above 3.0x sustained invalidates; the H2 2026 working-capital release management promised is the near test, with Q4 seasonally the strongest cash quarter (SEK 883m in Q4 2025).

- Organic growth: below 3 percent for two quarters is the alarm; below 2 percent for two consecutive quarters invalidates; the UK order book converting in H2 2026 and the Spanish strikes ending are the swing.
